title: Differential priority shedding and hedged fallback plans for regional dependency resilience
creator: Marin Ortega
description: Background: We observed several incidents where cross-region Redis/Kafka/DB degradations caused cascading latency and request loss for latency-sensitive routes (chat generation and short-lived embeddings). Current mitigation (regional failover to cold replicas + binary circuit breakers) results in large tail latency and customer-visible errors. Objective: define and implement a graded, priority-aware admission and fallback strategy that preserves SLOs for high-priority traffic while degrading lower-priority work gracefully. Scope: connection pooling changes, multi-tier circuit breaker behavior, probabilistic and deterministic load-shedding, hedged reads, and partial-response strategies across Redis, Kafka, and primary DBs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) High-priority routes (payment-check, auth) maintain 99.9th percentile latency within SLOs during simulated downstream saturation in two-region failure tests. 2) Low-priority routes see controlled rejection rates (configurable) with documented cost/quality tradeoffs. 3) No single tenant can cause global pool exhaustion; per-tenant soft quotas enforced. 4) Playbooks and runbook entries added; on-call can switch global degrade level in <2 minutes. 5) Automated canary for rollout with traffic shadowing and metrics dashboard.
design_decisions:
- Use a three-tier admission controller: PRIORITY (P0/P1), STANDARD (P2), BEST_EFFORT (P3). Admission controller applies per-region soft tokens and a shared emergency budget.
- Replace single global connection pool with region-scoped pools and an elastic governor that can 'strip' connections from BEST_EFFORT lanes deterministically when under pressure.
- Circuit breakers adopt multi-state hysteresis: CLOSED -> PROBING (limited hedged reads) -> OPEN (reject BEST_EFFORT) -> DEGRADED (serve stale or cached on allowed routes) -> RECOVER.
- Implement probabilistic shedding for standard routes using a weighted sampler keyed by tenant priority + recent error budget usage.
- Hedged read policy: for reads to regional replicas, issue a parallel read to a remote replica after a small adaptive delay (based on current percentile latencies) only for PRIORITY lanes.
- Partial-response mode: when DB is the bottleneck, respond with truncated or metadata-only payloads for BEST_EFFORT requests and include quality tags to the caller for client-side handling.
- Integrate KV cache warm and prefix reuse for top-n keys to reduce downstream fanout under surge.
implementation_notes:
- Engineering TODOs: 1) Admission controller library (Go) with token buckets per lane + optional global reserve. 2) Elastic governor: modify connection pool to support lane-weighted trimming and fast reallocation. 3) Circuit state machine + metrics (prometheus counters/gauges). 4) Hedged-read client wrapper with adaptive delay. 5) Feature flags for region-by-region rollouts.
- Tests: unit + integration harness that drives Redis/Kafka/DB latencies and saturation; failure injection for network partitions; end-to-end SLO verification harness.
- Metrics to add: per-lane rejection_rate, per-tenant connection_count, hedged_read_win_rate, degraded_response_fraction, redis_fanout_rate, kafka_publish_retries, db_stall_seconds.
- Dashboard: runtime-1.22 -> create 'Dependency Resilience' board with cross-region histograms and tenant heatmap.
- PRs to open: admission-controller repo, connection-pool-service, runtime-proxy client.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind canary for 5% of traffic (internal + smoke customers) in us-west1; shadow mode for hedged reads. Phase 1: enable admission controller for P0/P1 lane only, monitor 24h. Phase 2: activate lane trimming for BEST_EFFORT in two regions with synthetic high load. Phase 3: enable full policy globally and enable partial-response for selected workloads. Each phase gated by runbook checks and SLO regressions <2x baseline for non-P0 routes.
test_plan: 1) Chaos: inject 30-90s tail latency to primary DB and 20-50% packet loss to replica region; validate hedged reads reduce tail by >40% for PRIORITY. 2) Load: ramp to 5x baseline for 15 minutes to ensure BEST_EFFORT rejection rates are within configured thresholds. 3) Multi-region failover: simulate full region outage and validate global emergency budget behavior. 4) Tenant safety: run tenant-fairness suite to ensure no tenant exceeds soft quota during surge.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: false positives from probabilistic shedding could drop valuable customer work. Mitigation: start in shadow mode and tune sampler weights via offline replay.
- Risk: hedged reads increase overall resource usage. Mitigation: hedging only for PRIORITY lanes + adaptive delay to keep redundant calls minimal.
- Risk: complexity in pool reallocation could cause transient connection churn. Mitigation: implement graceful handoff and maintain short-lived spare pool to absorb churn.
- Risk: partial responses break downstream clients. Mitigation: only expose partial mode behind opt-in flags and include clear quality headers and client SDK support.
